Nethermind, for example, is written in C# and you can test with `dotnet test <project_name>` run in the appropriate directory (and with the appropriate build tools). ya i get that - but im saying - dont the major players have to coordinate to make sure that besu doesnt screw geth, etc? like all the clients have to work together in some test env before this goes live, no? anyway thatnks for the info i will look at that consensys 1559 repo shell as a starting point, thanks! I *think* (don't quote me on this as I'm not intimately involved) what happens is that each client builds their thing separately along with their own integration test suites. Then they join a test network together and they each run their own test suite against the shared test network. If anyone desyncs from the network, everyone looks to see what the cause of the problem was (which client has a bug) and then that client fixes, rejoins the network, and everyone runs their test suite again. Essentially, each time builds their client mostly in isolation from the other teams, with the exception of connecting up to a shared test network. Some EIPs have tests attached to them, but 1559 does not. yes - it's that shared test network that i am interested in getting connected to - along with whatever the source of the current clients are that are connecting to that network - it looks like <@!574864862338088960> is coordinating that so i will wait for his response and perhaps make a mention in ethereum magicians - i think this process should be a bit more documented and transparent for people new to the project <@!323626686170136577> it would also be helpful to get a feel for _what_ you are trying to test: we've had various setups for different types of tests. Earlier you mentioned the 2718/1559 integration. If that's what you are after, in geth, then that code just isn't ready yet, like I mentioned previously. If you just want to "run 1559", besu is probably best documented Like Micah mentioned, the way we are testing implementations is having them on a single network and gathering metrics on the various nodes, but each client has its own approach to do this. We're also planning to do load testing on that network whenever all clients have synced to the chain head. ok, I'm still going over all the links, will check out besu as well, thanks! hi guys, sorry for the questions; it's a bit hard to find stuff, and I do understand that things are fluid...is this document still valid? it seems old, not sure if the updates are current https://wiki.hyperledger.org/display/BESU/EIP-1559+testnet+guide <@!323626686170136577> All info to join the testnet are here: https://github.com/ConsenSys/eip1559-rhodes On Besu the implementation is available in master branch For Geth the reference implementation is: https://github.com/quilt/go-ethereum/tree/eip1559 For Nethermind it is available in 1.10.14 and higher Eth Stats: http://3.21.227.120:3001/ Block explorer: http://3.21.227.120:3000/ I have an npm command to join the testnet with Besu. Will update it to the latest version soon and send you the link. It is a one-liner command to run awesome, thanks!
